consequence.statement: The --probe flag behavior changes to return cached probe results instead of running synchronous probes; the flag is hidden and scheduled for removal in a future release.
consequence.remediation: Update monitoring or health check scripts that depend on synchronous probe execution via cilium-health status --probe; verify whether cached results are acceptable for your use case.

original.statement: The cilium-health status --probe flag no longer runs synchronous probes; it now returns cached results and is hidden, scheduled for removal in a future release.

consequence.statement: `cilium-health status --probe` still runs but no longer performs a synchronous probe. It returns the results of the most recent cached probe instead. The option is hidden and will be removed in a future release.
consequence.remediation: Check any scripts or health checks that call `cilium-health status --probe` and expect a fresh synchronous probe. Make sure cached results are acceptable, and plan to stop using the flag before it is removed.

corrected.statement: In Cilium 1.17, `cilium-health status --probe` no longer runs a synchronous probe. It is now a hidden option that returns the results of the most recent cached probe, and it will be removed in a future release.

decision.reason: [ev-5f4aedc964f4] says the synchronous probe via `cilium-health status --probe` is no longer supported in 1.17, and the option is now hidden and returns the most recent cached probe. So the command still works after the upgrade, but differently: it returns cached results instead of running a fresh probe. That makes the main consequence in this release behavior-change, not deprecation, because deprecation means the old behaviour still works today and breaks later. The planned future removal is extra context and does not change the review class.
